ai.title: Mitosis versus Meiosis
ai.subject: Physiology
ai.summary: Mitosis and meiosis are specialised cell division processes that generate identical somatic cells or haploid gametes. Understanding their regulation helps explain growth disorders, cancers and infertility, especially in low‑resource settings.

sections.p: Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells for growth, repair and asexual reproduction. Meiosis produces four genetically diverse haploid cells for sexual reproduction.

b: Prophase I: synapsis and crossing‑over → genetic diversity.
Metaphase I: homologues line up as pairs.
Meiosis II mirrors mitosis, separating sister chromatids.
sections.p: Both start with DNA replication (S phase). Mitosis proceeds through prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase. Meiosis adds a second division (Meiosis I and II) with homologous chromosome pairing and crossing‑over in prophase I.

b: G2/M checkpoint: DNA damage halts entry.
Spindle assembly checkpoint: prevents premature anaphase.
sections.p: Cyclins and cyclin‑dependent kinases (CDKs) drive both cycles, but meiosis adds meiosis‑specific regulators (e.g., Spo11 for DSB formation, MPF modulation). Checkpoints ensure DNA integrity before segregation.

b: Meiosis errors → nondisjunction → miscarriage, Down syndrome.
sections.p: Errors cause aneuploidy, tumorigenesis or infertility. In low‑resource settings, infections (e.g., malaria, HIV) can disrupt cell‑cycle proteins, increasing cancer risk.

b: High mitotic index on biopsy suggests aggressive tumour.
sections.p: Recognising when cell‑division pathways are abnormal guides diagnosis and therapy for cancers, congenital aneuploidies and infertility. Many chemotherapeutics target mitotic spindle formation.

t.b: How proliferative the tumour is; >10 mitoses/10 HPF indicates high grade.
Detects chromosomal number abnormalities; confirms trisomy 21 or Turner syndrome.
Rises appropriately if meiosis‑derived embryo is viable; plateau may signal miscarriage.

b: Mitosis vs meiosis: number of divisions, chromosome number of products.
Crossing‑over occurs only in meiosis I.
Chemotherapy agents (e.g., vincristine) target mitotic spindle.
sections.p: Focus on distinguishing features, clinical scenarios, and implications of drugs that affect division.

whenToSeekHelp: Rapidly enlarging mass with systemic symptoms (fever, weight loss) – suspect aggressive cancer.
Recurrent miscarriage after 2nd trimester – consider meiotic nondisjunction or parental chromosomal abnormalities.
